title: Transgender Symbol Emoji ⚧️ Meaning and How It's Used
description: The ⚧️ transgender symbol emoji combines gender signs into one emblem of trans identity and pride. Learn what it means, where it appears, and its flag link.
summary: The ⚧️ transgender symbol emoji merges the traditional male and female signs with a third, combined arm. It represents transgender people and communities. It is used in bios to express identity or allyship, in posts about trans rights and awareness days, and as a component of the transgender flag emoji.
meaning: ⚧️ is built from familiar parts. The circle with an arrow is the male sign, the circle with a cross is the female sign, and the third arm blends the two into an arrow with a crossbar. Joined on one circle, they form a symbol that has been used by transgender communities since the 1990s to represent gender identities beyond the one assigned at birth.

The emoji is primarily a marker of identity and solidarity. Trans people include it in bios and usernames, often near pronouns. Allies, clinics, support groups, and advocacy organizations use it to show that a space or resource is trans-inclusive. In posts it accompanies coming-out announcements, transition milestones, and discussions of gender-affirming care and legal rights.

It is closely tied to two annual observances: the International Transgender Day of Visibility on March 31, which celebrates trans lives, and the Transgender Day of Remembrance on November 20, which honors people killed in anti-trans violence. Use during Pride Month in June is also heavy. The tone ranges from celebratory to mournful depending on the occasion.

As a symbol of a group that is often targeted, ⚧️ also shows up in hostile contexts, used sarcastically by people opposing trans rights. That is a misuse and not its meaning. The emoji became available in 2020 together with the transgender flag, 🏳️‍⚧️, after years of requests from users and advocates.

contexts.label: In bios and usernames
contexts.body: A ⚧️ in a profile most often means the person is transgender, and sometimes that they are a committed ally or work in trans health or advocacy. It commonly sits beside pronouns, the trans flag, or 🏳️‍🌈. Treat it as information the person chose to share, not as an invitation to ask personal questions.

contexts.label: On awareness days
contexts.body: On March 31 and November 20, and throughout Transgender Awareness Week in mid November, organizations and individuals post ⚧️ with messages of support, statistics from named sources, and memorials. Brands that use it at these times are expected to back the gesture with real inclusion.

contexts.label: In health and community information
contexts.body: Clinics, helplines, student groups, and event organizers use the emoji to label trans-specific services, meetups, and resources, in the way ♿ marks accessibility. It helps people scanning a list find what applies to them quickly. Pride event programs and campus resource pages use it the same way, next to session titles or room listings.

confusedWith.difference: 🏳️‍⚧️ is the flag with light blue, pink, and white stripes. It is more colorful and more widely recognized. ⚧️ is the standalone emblem. Technically the flag emoji is built by combining a white flag with this symbol.
♀️ is the single female sign, a circle with a cross below, used for women and women's categories. ⚧️ carries three arms on one circle and refers to transgender identity specifically.
♂️ is the male sign, a circle with an arrow pointing up and to the right. It forms one part of the transgender symbol but by itself denotes men or male categories.

avoid: Do not use ⚧️ sarcastically or to mock someone's gender; that is harassment and violates most platform rules.
Avoid adding it next to another person's name to reveal or speculate that they are trans.
Do not use it as a generic "gender" or restroom icon when you mean all genders; say that in words.
design: A circle with three projections: an arrow toward the upper right, a cross pointing down, and a combined arrow with a crossbar toward the upper left. Depending on the platform it is shown as a bare symbol or in white on a colored square tile. Devices that predate its 2020 release may display an empty box.

faqs.q: What does ⚧️ mean in a bio?
faqs.a: Generally that the person is transgender. Some allies and professionals who serve the community also display it. If it matters for how you address them, follow the pronouns they list.

faqs.q: What do the three parts of the symbol mean?
faqs.a: One arm is the male sign's arrow, one is the female sign's cross, and the third fuses both. Together they represent people whose gender differs from the sex recorded at birth, including those who are neither exclusively male nor female.

faqs.q: How can I tell ⚧️ and 🏳️‍⚧️ apart?
faqs.a: ⚧️ is the symbol; 🏳️‍⚧️ is the transgender pride flag. They mean much the same, with the flag being more common in celebrations. Both were approved in 2020.

faqs.q: Why does ⚧️ show as a box or a flag plus a symbol on my device?
faqs.a: Older operating systems do not include the 2020 emoji. They show a blank box for ⚧️, and they break the flag into a white flag followed by the symbol. Updating your system resolves it.
